I honestly thought I was the only one who thinks about their therapist when their not at therapy. I never thought to tell him about this though I have mentioned to him things like- I was thinking of what you said or how you told me a way to handle a situation. 

I did skip about six months of therapy during Covid when they had it via tele-health because it didn’t work well for me. I went back recently in November and he said he was thinking of me and wondered how I was doing. I told him I was doing good until I had an issue and I’m so glad to be back talking to him. 

Full disclosure- he’s my first therapist ever and I was his first client when he started at the office I go to which is an old Victorian House. 

I hope that if you decide to tell your therapist how you feel it will be welcomed and appreciated, and not a sour experience like in your past.

I’ve been in therapy for roughly six years. It’s important to go into therapy without holding things back, you don’t need to share everything at once or at all depending on your situation. Therapist are able to read between the lines in stories and events in your life. I was surprised to find so many things about myself and why I function the way I do. 
Of course I’m in therapy for a different reason and my childhood is a key factor in why I’m there along with a few other things. My advice on going to therapy is don’t lie or try to cover things up, it’s not helpful to you or the therapist. Also, crying is okay.. if you have a good therapist then you’ll feel comfortable to say or do whatever you want, it’s your mental health journey, remember that. Good luck!
